events.title: Active Art for Toddlers
events.posterCredit: Kadist — Vinciane Lebrun / CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: Let the art adventures begin early! This playful, hands-on class is designed especially for our youngest artists. Together, children and their caregivers will use toys and familiar art tools to make this introduction to art extra fun. Painting with sponges, miniature cars, rollers and fingers all add to the hands-on experience and keep little hands and minds engaged. Our young artists will also have the chance to explore alternative activities that encourage social interaction and fine motor skills throughout each class. Participating toddlers must be accompanied by a participating adult. As with every art class, dress for a mess! Appropriate for toddlers 2 to 4 years, accompanied by a participating adult.

events.title: Adult Ballet
events.place: HARVEY MILK CENTER FOR THE ARTS
events.posterCredit: Duboce Park Landmark District — me / CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: This class is designed for adult dancers of all abilities. Students will continue to strengthen their ballet technique with exercises and combinations aimed to improve alignment and balance, strengthen muscles, and increase flexibility. Prior ballet experience is recommended.

events.title: All Ages Martial Arts Sampler - Advanced
events.address: 95 Justin Dr @ Murray St, San Francisco, CA
events.posterCredit: Wild Side West — Beatrice Murch / CC BY 2.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: Continuing instruction for advanced students in karate (ZBBKI purple belt or higher).

events.title: All Ages Martial Arts Sampler - Beginning
events.address: 95 Justin Dr @ Murray St, San Francisco, CA
events.posterCredit: Wild Side West — Beatrice Murch / CC BY 2.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: Traditional karate taught by experienced senseis.

events.title: Archery - Indoor Target League
events.posterCredit: Congregation Beth Sholom — Rburde / CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: A mixed format indoor archery league (Adults 20yds, Youth 10yds). The league is a great way to learn how to score with other archers of all ages, skill levels & bow styles. Bow categories are: Olympic Recurve, Barebow Recurve, Traditional, Compound Freestyle, and Compound Bowhunter. While usage of your own equipment is recommended, barebow recurve & barebow compound equipment is available for league use. League schedule is comprised of a 5-week season, followed by a finals competition. Awards will be given at season's end. Please contact joseph.arnaldo@sfgov.org for more information.

events.title: Archery After School
events.place: BETTY ANN ONG CHINESE REC CENTER
events.address: 1199 Mason St @ Washington St, San Francisco, CA
events.posterCredit: San Francisco Cable Car Museum — Jaredzimmerman (WMF) / CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: Introduce your child to the exciting world of indoor target archery with After School Archery! This program helps participants develop valuable skills like focus, self-control, and discipline, traits that benefit both on the range and in the classroom. The curriculum follows the NASP (National Archery in Schools Program) format, and all necessary equipment is provided.

events.title: Art and Animals
events.posterCredit: Randall Museum — Jllm06 / CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: Each week, a different animal is the star of our classroom. We learn fun facts and explore the wonders of these amazing creatures. Often, a live animal pays us a visit in person; other times we closely examine skeletons, taxidermy models, and habitats. Then, we get busy making art inspired by their unique characteristics. Projects, techniques and animal vary every session, but you can count on having fun, getting messy and learning something new every week. This hands-on class is as fun for the accompanying adults as it is for the kids. Class fee includes one child and one participating adult. Please register using the child's name.

events.title: Artist Workshop
events.posterCredit: Randall Museum — Jllm06 / CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: Get busy creating as we learn about, explore and practice with the exciting variety of mediums and tools in the Randall Museum's Art Studio. We'll workshop projects, techniques and creative approaches in every class and see where the process leads us!

events.title: Ashtanga Yoga and Hatha Yoga Fusion
events.posterCredit: Glen Canyon Park — Unknown author / Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: One was compiled around 200 BCE and other was oriented over 5000 years ago. One is the gift to humanity by Maharshi Patanjali which was then instituted by Swami Vivekanandji and the other by Swami Swatmaramaji in the form of his compilation viz. HathaYoga Pradipika. Let's gradually study Chakras and the practice of Body, Mind and Breath to fuse these year-old traditions for the exploration of the Self and Nature.

events.title: Asian Art Museum of San Francisco
events.titleEn: Asian Art Museum of San Francisco
events.place: Asian Art Museum of San Francisco
events.placeEn: Asian Art Museum of San Francisco
events.overview: The Asian Art Museum of San Francisco – Chong-Moon Lee Center for Asian Art and Culture is a museum in San Francisco, California, that specializes in Asian art. The museum building and its permanent collection are owned by the City of San Francisco.
events.overviewEn: The Asian Art Museum of San Francisco – Chong-Moon Lee Center for Asian Art and Culture is a museum in San Francisco, California, that specializes in Asian art. The museum building and its permanent collection are owned by the City of San Francisco.
events.overviewKo: 아시아 미술관은 미국 캘리포니아주 샌프란시스코에 있는 미술관이다. 올림픽 선수였던 에이버리 브런디지가 1960년대에 설립했다. 영구 소장품으로 18,000점 이상의 미술 작품을 소장하고 있으며, 그 중 일부는 6,000년이나 된 것이다.

events.title: Audio Production
events.address: 1800 Chestnut St @ Buchanan St, San Francisco, CA
events.posterCredit: Moscone Recreation Center — Ragesoss / CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: Explore the exciting world of audio production in this beginner-friendly class for youth! Participants will learn the fundamentals of creating and recording sound, including music production, sound effects, voice recording for podcasts, radio, and film, and basic audio editing techniques. Using microphones, keyboards, digital sequencers, and audio production software, students will create their own electronic music projects, record original sounds and dialogue, and learn the basics of mixing and sound design.Whether you're interested in making music, or creating movie-style sound effects, this hands-on class offers a fun and creative introduction to audio production. From GarageBand to Star Wars-inspired sound design, come make some noise—and learn how to capture it!

events.title: Ballroom Dance
events.address: 500 Felton St @ Holyoke St, San Francisco, CA
events.posterCredit: Portola, San Francisco — Haldean Brown from San Francisco, USA / CC BY-SA 2.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: Come join in on the fun! Bring your partner and glide across the dance floor during our Open Ballroom Dance sessions. These sessions are music based and no instruction is provided. Music is played by volunteers. Sign up for this fun, recreational dance program!

events.title: Body Worship
events.place: HARVEY MILK CENTER FOR THE ARTS
events.posterCredit: Duboce Park Landmark District — me / CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: Come lift your spirit and build physical confidence through movement and dance‑based exercise! This class features a 55‑minute warm‑up and cardio workout designed to strengthen your core, increase flexibility, and develop clean, confident technique. We’ll finish with 30 minutes of choreography inspired by an eclectic blend of styles, from Jazz and Contemporary to Voguing and Hip‑Hop. The goal is simple: leave every class feeling empowered, sassy, and full of self‑love. Join us and groove it out!

events.title: BollyX
events.place: HARVEY MILK CENTER FOR THE ARTS
events.posterCredit: Duboce Park Landmark District — me / CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: BollyX is perfect for anyone looking to dance to Bollywood music, get their heart rate up, and spread more joy in the world! BollyX is a Bollywood-inspired cardio dance-fitness program that combines dynamic choreography with music from around the world.

events.title: California Academy of Sciences
events.address: 55 Music Concourse Drive, San Francisco, CA 94118
events.overview: The California Academy of Sciences is a research institute and natural history museum in San Francisco, California, that is among the largest museums of natural history in the world, housing over 46 million specimens. The academy began in 1853 as a learned society and still carries out a large amount of original research. The institution is located in Golden Gate Park on the West Side of San Francisco. Completely rebuilt in 2008, the academy's primary building in Golden Gate Park covers 400,000 square feet.

The academy began in 1853 as a learned society and still carries out a large amount of original research. The institution is located in Golden Gate Park on the West Side of San Francisco. Completely rebuilt in 2008, the academy's primary building in Golden Gate Park covers 400,000 square feet.

events.title: Casting in Bronze
events.address: Golden Gate Park, San Francisco, CA
events.posterCredit: Outside Lands — Not stated / Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: Learn the organic metal art of lost wax casting. This course will cover the process by which metal object is cast from a wax model, allowing you to see the limitless forms that metal can take. The class starts by showing you how to work with wax (hot and cold) to create pieces of jewelry that will be cast. The class fee covers the cost of basic materials (including bronze). Each student will be given one 2 1/2 inch flask to fit their wax designs in. Students who wish to work in silver are responsible for purchasing sterling silver which will be covered in class. Instructor will be doing the castings for the students. Beginners are welcome. The Jewelry Studio is located on the upper floor, with stair access only. For accommodations requests or accessibility questions, please contact rpdaccess@sfgov.org or 415-831-6841. Please note that submitting your request at least two weeks before…

events.title: Ceramics - Sharon Art Studio
events.address: Golden Gate Park, San Francisco, CA
events.posterCredit: Outside Lands — Not stated / Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: This class introduces hand building techniques including pinch, coil, and slab construction, and basic wheel throwing techniques of wedging, centering, throwing cups and bowls, and trimming. Instructor provides individual guidance for all skill levels. Surface decoration and glazing techniques will also be explored. Clay is available for purchase at the studio with a 100-pound clay limit per session. No outside clay or glazes allowed. Students must purchase a basic pottery tool kit prior to the first day of class. Suggested materials list can be found at sharonartstudio.org. Students may enroll in only one ceramics class per session. Note: New students (new to ceramics or Sharon Art Studio) must attend the first three classes. All skill levels welcome.

events.title: Ceramics Open Studio
events.address: Golden Gate Park, San Francisco, CA
events.posterCredit: Outside Lands — Not stated / Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: For enrolled ceramics students at the Sharon Art Studio who want more, we offer Open Studio! Students can practice wheel throwing, hand building, and glaze or trim their pieces. There is no instruction given during open studio time. All firing is done by instructor without an additional charge. All participants MUST be enrolled in a ceramics course in order to register for open studio. Please note, registration for open studio is done at Sharon Art Studio only, no online registration available.

events.title: Ceramics: Tween/Teen Ceramics
events.address: Golden Gate Park, San Francisco, CA
events.posterCredit: Outside Lands — Not stated / Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: This class is accessible to all skill levels and offers the opportunity to try a variety of ceramic techniques. We’ll explore hand building, throwing on the wheel, surface texture, and glazing. Materials are included in the price of the class.

events.title: Chinese Classical Dance
events.address: 500 Felton St @ Holyoke St, San Francisco, CA
events.posterCredit: Portola, San Francisco — Haldean Brown from San Francisco, USA / CC BY-SA 2.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: Chinese classical dance includes movements and postures from other artistic forms such as Chinese folk dance and martial arts. Focusing on the breath, it is displayed with finesse, elegance, and the controlled expression of strength and power.

events.title: Chinese Folk Dance
events.place: HARVEY MILK CENTER FOR THE ARTS
events.posterCredit: Duboce Park Landmark District — me / CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: Learn the fundamentals for Chinese folk dance including native traditional Chinese dance and international folk dances. Lessons will focus on learning basic steps while improving balance and strength. Please wear comfortable shoes and clothing.

events.title: Chinese Music Appreciation
events.address: 500 Felton St @ Holyoke St, San Francisco, CA
events.posterCredit: Portola, San Francisco — Haldean Brown from San Francisco, USA / CC BY-SA 2.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: Music lovers are welcome to join our choir! The goal of this choir is to enrich senior adult recreation by participating in Chinese music appreciation and improving singing skills. A volunteer will lead the choir in training, teaching students the music theory knowledge, vocal skills, and a variety of Chinese art songs, eventually integrating all elements into the choir practice.

events.title: Contemporary Jewish Museum
events.overview: The Contemporary Jewish Museum is a non-collecting museum at 736 Mission Street at Yerba Buena Lane in the South of Market neighborhood of San Francisco, California. The museum, which was founded in 1984, is located in the historic Jessie Street Substation, which was gutted and its interior redesigned by Daniel Libeskind, along with a new addition; the new museum opened in 2008. The museum's mission is to make the diversity of the Jewish experience relevant for a 21st- century audience through exhibitions and educational programs. The executive director is Kerry King.
events.overviewEn: The Contemporary Jewish Museum is a non-collecting museum at 736 Mission Street at Yerba Buena Lane in the South of Market neighborhood of San Francisco, California. The museum, which was founded in 1984, is located in the historic Jessie Street Substation, which was gutted and its interior redesigned by Daniel Libeskind, along with a new addition; the new museum opened in 2008. The museum's mission is to make the diversity of the Jewish experience relevant for a 21st- century audience through exhibitions and educational programs. The executive director is Kerry King.

events.title: Creative Art Discovery
events.posterCredit: Kadist — Vinciane Lebrun / CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: Unleash your imagination and explore the world of art through hands-on projects. This class is for young artists who like to experiment, create and discover new techniques and get inspired by being around other young artists. From painting and drawing, sculpture and mixed media, students can experiment with both traditional and unconventional art materials. Students will explore color, shape, and texture while developing their creativity, problem-solving & confidence in their art!

events.title: Creative Flow: Art for Everyone
events.posterCredit: Randall Museum — Jllm06 / CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: This beginner-friendly, mixed media art class invites adults to explore and have fun with the creative process. Experience a variety of materials and techniques in a supportive and friendly space where process is valued over product. No experience needed, just curiosity and a willingness to create and unwind. Dress for a mess!

events.title: Creative Visual Art
events.posterCredit: Kadist — Vinciane Lebrun / CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: Come have some fun in this ultimate creative arts class which combines both imagination and inspiration from real-world images. We will be inventing imaginary scenes, creating intricate abstract works of art, and making the mundane extraordinary using both drawing and painting techniques. On our journey we will explore some of the elements and principles of art, which are foundational pillars of a visual arts education. This class aids in the development of visual art skills, which can help prepare students for entering visual arts high schools and beyond.

events.title: Creative Worlds Studio: Imaginative Art
events.posterCredit: Kadist — Vinciane Lebrun / CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: Students will create imaginary scenes, transform everyday objects into abstract art, and explore mixed-media projects in drawing, painting, collage, and light sculpture, all while building strong visual storytelling and foundational art skills for secondary visual arts education.

events.title: Drawing Practice
events.address: Golden Gate Park, San Francisco, CA
events.posterCredit: Outside Lands — Not stated / Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: Come experience fine art drawing. This class is a focused space for observational drawing practice in the fine art tradition. Subjects include a mix of figure, still life, and landscape (weather permitting). #INKTOBER will be observed with a special section on ink drawing during October dates. On-the-spot instruction will be provided. Music will be played during class. Classes wrap with a brief mini show for reflection and friendly feedback. Please bring your preferred materials to class. No fume producing materials please (turpentines, spray fixatives indoors, etc.). Please bring requested materials to class. Materials list available at sharonartstudio.org.

events.title: Dynamic Duo Clay Explorers
events.posterCredit: Randall Museum — Jllm06 / CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: Discover the wonders of clay with your small child. Together you'll get your hands into this wonderfully tactile medium. Roll coils, build with slabs, pinch pots, and paint on glazes. You can make projects together that neither one of you could do alone. Registration fee includes one child and one adult. Each child must be accompanied by a participating adult. Please register for class using the child's name.

events.title: Exploration in Clay
events.posterCredit: Kadist — Vinciane Lebrun / CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: Discover the creative possibilities of working with clay in this comprehensive ceramics class. Participants will explore a variety of techniques, including hand-building, wheel throwing, surface decoration, and glazing, while learning the fundamentals of ceramic design and construction.Beginning students will build a strong foundation in clay processes and studio practices, while more experienced artists will receive individualized guidance to develop their own techniques, creative vision, and personal projects. Whether you're new to ceramics or looking to expand your skills, this class offers a supportive environment for artistic exploration and growth.All levels are welcome.

events.title: Exploratorium
events.overview: The Exploratorium is a museum of science, technology, and arts in San Francisco, California. Founded by physicist and educator Frank Oppenheimer in 1969, the museum was originally in the Palace of Fine Arts where it founded Pi Day in 1988. The museum relocated in 2013 to Piers 15 and 17 on San Francisco's waterfront. The museum has over 1,000 participatory exhibits divided into several galleries, mainly separated by content.

events.title: Fencing
events.address: 1800 Chestnut St @ Buchanan St, San Francisco, CA
events.posterCredit: Moscone Recreation Center — Ragesoss / CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: Learn the art of fencing, a truly elegant sport that has historical roots dating back to the 12th Century and has been featured at every one of the modern day Olympic games. Kids learn discipline, keep fit, and learn to strive to achieve excellence in a respectful & safe environment. All the equipment is provided. Kids should dress in athletic clothing and bring water.

events.placeEn: Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco
events.overview: The Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco, comprising the de Young Museum in Golden Gate Park and the Legion of Honor in Lincoln Park, is the largest public arts institution in the city of San Francisco. events.title: Girls Play Sports: Archery
events.address: 301 Naglee St @ Cayuga St, San Francisco, CA
events.posterCredit:
Cayuga Park — Orin Zebest

Camera location37° 42′ 49.69″ N, 122° 27′ 00.73″ W View this and… / CC BY 2.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: Ready, set, shoot! This archery course is designed just for girls who want to build their skills, grow their confidence, and have a blast doing it. Following the USA Archery curriculum, you'll learn how to shoot safely and accurately while mastering proper form, scoring basics, and range etiquette. Each session includes fun games, friendly challenges, and empowering instruction in a supportive, all-girls environment. Whether you're brand new or aiming to improve, this class is your target for fun and growth. All equipment is provided; just bring your focus and fierce energy!

events.title: Hatha Yoga and Ashtanga Yoga Fusion
events.posterCredit: Kadist — Vinciane Lebrun / CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: A Yoga style from Mind to Body and it’s a step to Hatha Yoga which says from Body to Mind. In addition, with a yoga practice of Fusion Yoga - Ashtang (Eight Limbs) Yoga and Hatha Yoga.

events.title: International Folk Dance
events.place: HARVEY MILK CENTER FOR THE ARTS
events.posterCredit: Duboce Park Landmark District — me / CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: Come learn Folk Dances from around the world. Note that we are listed as a senior class, but ALL AGES ARE WELCOME (18+)! We encourage all experience levels from beginners to long-time dancers to join us. We learn a variety of dances: circle, line, set, couples, trios - and more! Research shows that dance helps maintain balance and brain health. Our Dance Circle is an ongoing class and is a member of the Folk Dance Federation of Northern California. For more information contact Barbara Duhl bduhl@hotmail.com.

events.title: Intro to Origami
events.posterCredit: Kadist — Vinciane Lebrun / CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: Explore the ancient art of paper folding. Using just a simple sheet of paper, students will create fun origami animals, flowers, boxes, paper airplanes, and geometric shapes. Along the way, they’ll build confidence, focus, and fine motor skills through hands-on creativity. Each week builds on techniques learned in previous classes, helping students progress from beginner folds to lower-intermediate models like the traditional origami crane. No experience necessary.

events.title: Intro to Pilates - Yoga Fusion
events.address: 160 Mrs. Jackson Way, San Francisco, CA
events.posterCredit: John McLaren Park — SFHistoryNerd / CC0 (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: Wake up your body to focus your mind! This class is ideal for those in midlife and beyond who want to regain their vitality. You will learn techniques that increase flexibility, enhance posture, improve balance, and lower stress levels. Rediscover long-forgotten muscles and calm the mind with low-impact Hatha Yoga followed by beginner Mat Pilates exercises. Pilates more actively engages and stabilizes your core, and a strong core leads to better health! The class ends with a guided relaxation. ***Participants must be able to get down and up from the floor.***

events.title: Introduction to Inkjet Printing
events.posterCredit: Duboce Park Landmark District — me / CC BY-SA 3.0 (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: Take your images beyond the screen and into print. This course focuses on developing a cohesive body of work through the art of fine art and photographic printing. Participants will learn best practices for image selection, editing, color management, print preparation, and archival storage techniques to ensure long-lasting, high-quality prints.The class utilizes the Epson Stylus Pro, a professional inkjet printer capable of producing exceptional prints on a variety of media. Participants will gain hands-on experience preparing and printing their own photographs while exploring the creative and technical considerations of the printing process.A working knowledge of Adobe Photoshop and/or Lightroom is strongly recommended. Participants should bring a laptop with a current version of Adobe Photoshop or Lightroom installed, along with a thumb drive. Two 8x10 prints are included in the…

events.title: Jewelry Open Studio
events.address: Golden Gate Park, San Francisco, CA
events.posterCredit: Outside Lands — Not stated / Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
events.overview: Please Note: In order to register for open studio, you must be currently enrolled in a Sharon Art Studio a beginner or intermediate jewelry class that is 5 weeks or longer.* This open studio provides space and equipment for students to work independently to complete jewelry projects. Experience with studio equipment and safety protocols is necessary. Minimal instruction is provided. A jewelry monitor will be available to help answer questions and ensure proper safety precautions are taken with studio equipment. Please Note: The Jewelry Studio is located on the upper floor, with stair access only. For accommodations requests or accessibility questions, please contact rpdaccess@sfgov.org or 415-831-6841. stops.title: Transamerica Pyramid
stops.text: The Transamerica Pyramid Center is a pyramid-shaped 48-story modernist skyscraper in San Francisco, California, United States, and the second tallest building in the San Francisco skyline. Located at 600 Montgomery Street between Clay and Washington Streets in the city's Financial District, it was the tallest building in San Francisco from its completion in 1972 until 2017. The building no longer houses the headquarters of the Transamerica Corporation, which moved its U.S. headquarters to Baltimore, Maryland. The building is still associated with the company by being depicted on the company's logo. Designed by architects William Pereira and Harry D. Som, and built by Hathaway Dinwiddie Construction Company, the building stands at 853 feet.

stops.title: 345 California Center
stops.text: 345 California Center is a 48-story office tower in the financial district of San Francisco, California. Completed in 1986, the 211.8 m tower is the fifth tallest in the city after the Salesforce Tower, Transamerica Pyramid, 181 Fremont, and 555 California Street if the spires are included. It was originally proposed to be 30 m taller. The building was developed by Norland Properties, a private real estate investment firm led by Hany Ben-Halim. 345 California is in the middle of a block with historic buildings on each of the four corners.

stops.title: 555 California Street
stops.text: 555 California Street, formerly Bank of America Center, is a 52-story 779 ft skyscraper in San Francisco, California. It is the fourth tallest building in the city as of February 2021, and in 2013 was the largest by floor area. Completed in 1969, the tower was the tallest building west of the Mississippi River until the completion of the Transamerica Pyramid in 1972, and the world headquarters of Bank of America until the 1998 merger with NationsBank, when the company moved its headquarters to the Bank of America Corporate Center in Charlotte, North Carolina. It is currently owned by Vornado Realty Trust and The Trump Organization.
stops.textKo: 555 캘리포니아 스트리트는 미국 샌프란시스코에 위치한 마천루이다.

stops.title: Gerald Ford assassination attempt in San Francisco
stops.text: In San Francisco on September 22, 1975, Sara Jane Moore attempted to assassinate the 38th president of the United States, Gerald Ford, after he had made an address to the World Affairs Council. Moore tried to shoot President Ford with a .38 Special revolver. Her single shot missed, and a bystander prevented another shot by grabbing her shooting arm. Ford had survived a previous assassination attempt 17 days earlier; after this second attempt, he wore a bulletproof trench coat while out in public. On January 15, 1976, Moore was sentenced to life in prison for the attempt, and was released on parole on December 31, 2007.
stops.textKo: 1975년 9월 22일 샌프란시스코에서 사라 제인 무어가 미국 대통령 제럴드 포드가 세계문제협의회에서 연설을 마친 후 그를 암살하려고 시도했다. 무어는 .38 스페셜 리볼버로 포드 대통령을 저격하려 했다. 그녀가 쏜 단발은 빗나갔고, 한 구경꾼이 그녀의 사격하는 팔을 붙잡아 추가 발사를 막았다. 포드는 17일 전 발생했던 이전 암살 시도에서 살아남았으며, 이 두 번째 시도 이후 대중 앞에 나설 때는 방탄 트렌치코트를 착용했다. 1976년 1월 15일, 무어는 암살 미수 혐의로 종신형을 선고받았으며 2007년 12월 31일에 가석방되었다.

stops.title: San Francisco Museum of Modern Art
stops.text: The San Francisco Museum of Modern Art is a modern and contemporary art museum and nonprofit organization located in San Francisco, California. SFMOMA was the first museum on the West Coast devoted solely to 20th-century art, and has built an internationally recognized collection with over 33,000 works of painting, sculpture, photography, architecture, design, and media arts. The collection is displayed in 170,000 square feet of exhibition space, making the museum one of the largest in the United States overall, and one of the largest in the world for modern and contemporary art. In 2024, SFMOMA was ranked 14th in The Washington Post's list of the best art museums in the U.S. The museum was founded in 1935 with galleries in the Veterans Building in Civic Center. In 1995, the museum opened in its Mario Botta-designed home in the SoMa district.

stops.text: The George R. Moscone Convention Center, popularly known as the Moscone Center, is the largest convention and exhibition complex in San Francisco, California, United States. The complex consists of three main halls spread out across three blocks and 87 acres in the South of Market neighborhood. The convention center originally opened in 1981. It is named after former San Francisco mayor George Moscone, who was assassinated in November 1978.

stops.title: Room 641A
stops.text: Room 641A is a telecommunication interception facility operated by AT&T for the U.S. National Security Agency, as part of an American mass surveillance program. The facility commenced operations in 2003, and its purpose was publicly revealed by AT&T technician Mark Klein in 2006.

stops.title: Coit Tower
stops.text: Coit Tower is a 210-foot tower in the Telegraph Hill neighborhood of San Francisco, California, overlooking the city and San Francisco Bay. The tower, in the city's Pioneer Park, was built between 1932 and 1933 using Lillie Hitchcock Coit's bequest to beautify the city of San Francisco. It was added to the National Register of Historic Places on January 29, 2008. The Art Deco tower, built of unpainted reinforced concrete, was designed by architects Arthur Brown Jr. and Henry Temple Howard.

stops.title: California Academy of Sciences
stops.text: The California Academy of Sciences is a research institute and natural history museum in San Francisco, California, that is among the largest museums of natural history in the world, housing over 46 million specimens. The academy began in 1853 as a learned society and still carries out a large amount of original research. The institution is located in Golden Gate Park on the West Side of San Francisco. Completely rebuilt in 2008, the academy's primary building in Golden Gate Park covers 400,000 square feet. In early 2020, before the COVID-19 pandemic, the California Academy of Sciences had around 500 employees and an annual revenue of about $33 million.

stops.title: M. H. de Young Memorial Museum
stops.text: The de Young Museum, formally the M. H. de Young Memorial Museum, is a fine arts museum located in San Francisco, California, United States, named for early San Francisco newspaperman M. H. de Young. Located on the West Side of the city in Golden Gate Park, it is a component of the Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco, along with the Legion of Honor. The museum received 999,645 visitors in 2023, ranking as the 22nd most-visited museum in the United States, and the 82nd most-visited art museum in the world.

stops.title: Contemporary Jewish Museum
stops.text: The Contemporary Jewish Museum is a non-collecting museum at 736 Mission Street at Yerba Buena Lane in the South of Market neighborhood of San Francisco, California. The museum, which was founded in 1984, is located in the historic Jessie Street Substation, which was gutted and its interior redesigned by Daniel Libeskind, along with a new addition; the new museum opened in 2008. The museum's mission is to make the diversity of the Jewish experience relevant for a 21st- century audience through exhibitions and educational programs. The executive director is Kerry King. The museum closed in December 2024 due to financial problems, and in 2026 announced that it would sell its building to provide funds.

stops.title: Museum of the African Diaspora
stops.text: The Museum of the African Diaspora is a contemporary art museum in San Francisco, California. MoAD holds exhibitions and presents artists exclusively of the African diaspora, one of only a few museums of its kind in the United States. Located at 685 Mission St. and occupying the first three floors of the St. Regis Museum Tower in the Yerba Buena Arts District, MoAD is a nonprofit organization as well as a Smithsonian Affiliate.

events.title: USS Pampanito
events.overview: USS Pampanito is a Balao-class submarine built for the United States Navy during World War II; it is the third U.S. Navy vessel named for the pompano fish. She completed six war patrols from 1944 to 1945 and served as a United States Naval Reserve training ship from 1960 to 1971. She is now a National Historic Landmark, preserved as a memorial and museum ship in the San Francisco Maritime National Park Association located at Fisherman's Wharf in San Francisco, California.

YBCA programs year-round in two landmark buildings—the Galleries and Forum by Japanese architect Fumihiko Maki and the adjacent Theater by American architect James Stewart Polshek and Todd Schliemann. Betti-Sue Hertz served as Curator from 2008 through 2015.
